messages:
Casey (support): Priya from AcmeCorp reporting a sharp p95/p99 latency regression over the last 30m, integrated via our hosted API. They say normal p99 ~2s, now seeing spikes to 18-22s and many 504s. They attached curl and sample trace.
Priya (customer): yes — it started after a traffic spike from a batch job on our side (we retried a bunch of requests). We can pause but need guidance for repro. here is the minimal curl we used:
```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd-3-small","input":"hi"}'```
Casey (support): thanks, we suspect admission control/backpressure. tagging eng-sre + eng-runtime — @Marta @Noah can you take a look? Customer is on paid plan, high priority. They reported ~600 RPS bursts for short periods.
Marta (eng-sre): looking. grabbing metrics: linking grafana panel for request queue depth and worker utilization — https://grafana/redwood/d/request-queues?orgId=1&var-tenant=acmecorp
Marta (eng-sre): initial read: cluster shows sustained queue length rising around 2026-11-08T14:10Z. Worker GPU utilization is high but not pegged, CPU on control plane spiky. Admission throttle started dropping requests to the secondary tier ~14:12Z. p99 correlates with queue depth climbs.
Noah (eng-runtime): logs from runtime admission controller show long wait times in admit path. snippet:
```
[admit] tenant=acmecorp queue_wait_ms=12500 workers_busy=32/32 route=rwd-3-small
[worker] kv_cache_miss=0.48 batch_size=8 inflight_requests=96
```
Noah (eng-runtime): looks like a combination of high concurrency from a single tenant plus large batch footprints causing KV cache thrash and worker slot exhaustion.
Sam (oncall): any recent deploys? @Dev Deploy Bot did any canaries land in last hour?
Dev Deploy Bot: Canary for runtime/prefix-cache-fix passed at 2026-11-08T13:55Z. No rollouts since. No config changes to admission thresholds.
Marta (eng-sre): important note: tenant has no aggressive rate limiting at edge; their SDK retried with parallelism 50 which amplified queueing. we see many short-lived connections.
Casey (support): Priya — can you temporarily throttle parallelism on your side to 8-10 and retest? if you can pause the batch job that triggered it, that will help us confirm.
Priya (customer): we can pause for 15m. pausing now.
Marta (eng-sre): while the customer pauses, trying mitigations: 1) temporarily increase per-tenant concurrent slots for AcmeCorp from 32 -> 48 (on Dedicated we can, on Hosted we have soft caps). 2) enable tenant-specific token-bucket at edge to smooth bursts. 3) fall back to rwd-3-micro variant for non-critical routes. I'm going to test increasing concurrency on the runtime pool.
Noah (eng-runtime): running the scale command now:
```bash
# increase tenant slots (dry-run)
redwoodctl tenants update acmecorp --concurrency-slots 48 --apply-temp 15m
```
Noah (eng-runtime): applied. watching queue metrics.
Marta (eng-sre): queue depth dropped ~40% after slot bump but p99 still elevated ~8s (was 20s). reasoning: large number of tiny requests are still creating more work due to context init and KV cache cold-starts per request pattern.
Noah (eng-runtime): also enabling prefix caching on that worker pool to reduce repeated compute: toggling fast-kv-cache=true for pool acme-prod. applying.
Dev Deploy Bot: Feature toggle fast-kv-cache=true applied to pool acme-prod. Rolling config to 6 nodes.
Noah (eng-runtime): config rolled, seeing fewer KV misses, batch sizes stabilized around 6.
Priya (customer): latency improving on our side, p99 down to ~3.1s after pausing. good progress.
Marta (eng-sre): good. still need to prevent recurrence. short term mitigation plan: 1) keep temporary concurrency bump for 30m 2) enable per-tenant smoothing token-bucket set to 200 req/s burst 300 with refill 200/s 3) add a short-circuit fallback to rwd-3-micro for requests detected coming from high-concurrency SDKs.
Sam (oncall): I'll put an emergency policy on billing/usage so the customer's spike won't cause unexpected charges while we sort config.
Casey (support): Priya — to help prevent this in future: please use SDK recommended concurrency <=12 for generation endpoints. we'll also send a short recommended config snippet.
Casey (support): recommended snippet:
```js
// recommended concurrency limiter
const limiter = new Semaphore(12)
await limiter.acquire()
try { await client.generate(...) } finally { limiter.release() }
```
Priya (customer): we'll add. thanks. can you confirm whether retries should have backoff?
Marta (eng-sre): yes — exponential backoff with jitter, don't retry 5xx without backoff. Also prefer rate-limited queuing instead of parallel retries. We'll follow up with an RFC on SDK changes.
Noah (eng-runtime): follow-up technical notes for the team: root cause summary: tenant flood of concurrent small requests + lack of edge smoothing -> admission controller saturated workers -> KV cache thrash and smaller effective batch sizes -> increased queue wait time and p99 spikes. Key logs:
```
[admit] tenant=acmecorp queue_len=124 queue_wait_p99_ms=18734
[worker] inflight=96 batch_avg=4 kv_cache_hit=0.52
```
Noah (eng-runtime): longer-term mitigations: - stronger tenant-level smoothing (token-bucket by path), - per-client connection concurrency limits at edge, - adaptive batch-sizing to prioritize throughput under KV thrash, - rapid fallback routing to cheaper micro model when latency SLOs are in danger.
Marta (eng-sre): action items: 
- Sam: keep temp concurrency increase until 15:15Z and monitor.
- Noah: schedule a follow-up config to make token-bucket persistent for tenant.
- Casey: send post-incident guidance to customer including SDK snippet + suggested retry backoff.
- Engineering: run a short chaos test on high-concurrency small-request pattern to validate admission heuristics.
Sam (oncall): monitoring alert thresholds adjusted: p99 > 5s for 3m will page eng-sre. added dashboard widgets for tenant-level queues.
Dev Deploy Bot: Canary rollback not needed. No further deploys planned.
Casey (support): Priya, do you want a follow-up call with SE to discuss SDK changes and queuing best practices? can do a short 30m session.
Priya (customer): yes please — would like to sync tomorrow morning PST. thanks for rapid help everyone.
Marta (eng-sre): marking this thread 'investigated' — will create a postmortem draft and link nightly. core conclusion: client-driven concurrency spike + insufficient smoothing at the edge caused request pile-ups; mitigations applied and customer paused spike. Postmortem will include prevention steps and SDK guidance.
Noah (eng-runtime): dropping a short repro we used so infra can simulate:
```bash
# repro: fire many tiny requests in parallel
for i in {1..1000}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx' -d '{"input":"ping"}' &
done
wait
```
Noah (eng-runtime): please don't run against prod without coordination :facepalm:
Casey (support): closing from support side for now; will reopen if latency creeps back up. thanks all :thumbsup:
